solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hangover from mixing rosé with some beer

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the wine's letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the wine, accent dropped, as raw letters
the froth on top of a poured beer is some of it

explanation.surface: A drinker blames the morning headache on having mixed rosé with beer the night before.
explanation.walkthrough: SOREHEAD is a sore head, the throbbing aftermath of a heavy night; the surface is about a hangover and so is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorehead is an informal term for the throbbing headache felt after excessive drinking the previous evening.

clue.text: Inadequate villain covered by broadcaster

indicators.note: something covered by another is enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
an imp is a little rascal

explanation.surface: A weak baddie is given airtime by a TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means meagre or insufficient in quantity, lacking what is needed.

clue.text: Rubbish good for small shelter

indicators.note: one thing for another means putting it in the other's place

parts.note: refuse is waste
G is the abbreviation for good
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Junk serves well enough as a small hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small shelter' reads as one phrase; 'small' belongs to the wordplay and 'shelter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of safety offering protection from danger or trouble.

clue.text: Top drink's available

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a shandy is beer mixed with lemonade

explanation.surface: The best drinks are on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning best; it is a verb meaning behead. A shandy is a British pub drink of beer and lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is conveniently close at hand and ready to use when needed.

clue.text: Turn half a degree holder of spur

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage

indicators.note: only half of the word is wanted, so its first half is dropped

parts.note: a graduate holds a university degree

explanation.surface: Rotate a riding spur's mount by half a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half a degree' reads like an angle; 'half' applies to 'a degree holder' and keeps its back half.
explanation.definitionFit: To actuate is to set in motion or prompt into action, which is what spurring someone on does.

clue.text: Starts to pursue overseas trade agreement to optimise source of chips

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, which are the only ones kept

parts.words: pursue overseas trade agreement to optimise
parts.note: the initial letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A business plan about chasing a foreign trade deal to make the most of a supply of microchips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' suggests silicon in a trade surface; here they are fried strips of a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips (fries in America) are cut from this tuber, so it is literally where they come from.

clue.text: Balls on fire go too far

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls
to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: Throwing burning balls sends them past the target.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to miss a target by passing beyond it, exceeding the intended point.

clue.text: Apt to follow fuss about right kind

definitions.note: a loose sense: sweet-natured and lovable

indicators.note: to follow means come after, so this piece is placed at the end of the others

parts.note: ado is fuss, the familiar pairing as in Much Ado About Nothing
R is the abbreviation for right
apt to do something is able to do it

explanation.surface: Something suitable comes after a fuss over the correct sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apt to follow' places ABLE after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable describes someone sweet and lovable, the warm-hearted sort of person one might call kind.

clue.text: Not even women take half-wits' left-overs

indicators.note: taking half of each word means one half is removed and the remaining half kept

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Odd women take the scraps left by fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-wits' looks like fools; the hyphen hides 'half' working on 'wits', and on 'women' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are bits and pieces remaining after the main part has been used or sold.

clue.text: Space for a pool

definitions.note: describes a kind of pool, so works as a modifier
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word for a pool whose edge seems to vanish into the horizon

explanation.walkthrough: An infinity pool is a swimming pool built so its water appears to run on into the view beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbounded space stretches without end, and the same word names a swimming pool with a vanishing edge.

clue.text: Further over there, covered with litter

indicators.note: something covered has another thing laid around it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: litter is straw bedding for animals
yon is an old word for that place over there

explanation.surface: A spot further off is covered in rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' reads as rubbish but means animal bedding, which wraps around the old word for 'over there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond describes something lying further away, past a given point in space or degree.

clue.text: Slide for small child

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A playground slide meant for a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: To skid is to slip sideways uncontrollably over a surface, as a car does on ice.

clue.text: Pop outlaw into small park with stash

definitions.note: a stash is the money; the answer is the box holding it

indicators.note: putting things into something places them inside its two ends

parts.note: the abbreviation for park
Iggy Pop is the punk singer, so Pop's first name
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A dad hides a fugitive in a little park along with a hidden hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a father or a bang; it calls up the punk rocker Iggy Pop, so it stands for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's savings box shaped like a pig is where a small hoard of coins gets kept.

clue.text: Bar room

definitions.note: as in space bar, the long keyboard key
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the long key on a keyboard that this word names

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar room' suggests a pub's saloon; split it, and each word separately leads to the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The space bar is the keyboard's widest key, and having space means having room to move.

clue.text: Man maybe steeped in his lechery

indicators.note: something steeped in a liquid lies wholly within it, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: runs across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps, is soaked in his own lust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as a male person, but it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea; 'maybe' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so it is one example of an island.

clue.text: Plot curve describing party at length

parts.note: an S is a curving bend, from the letter's shape
the Tory party is Britain's Conservatives
a line is a length, as of rope or text

explanation.surface: A graph's curve tracks a political party over a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot curve' looks like drawing a graph; 'Plot' is the noun for a story's events.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyline is the sequence of events that forms a narrative, the same thing as a plot.

clue.text: A little bit of rainfall allowed

parts.note: to fall is to drop
allowed means let

explanation.surface: A modest amount of rainfall has been permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' does double duty: it ends the definition and also supplies the first half of the wordplay, with 'allowed' the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tiny bead of water is the smallest unit a shower is made of.

clue.text: Bath content to appoint party whips as their elected representatives in capitals

indicators.note: capitals are the capital letters that begin each word, so only those are kept

parts.words: to appoint party whips as their elected representatives
parts.note: the opening letter of each of these eight words

explanation.surface: A Westminster story: the party of Bath gets to choose its own whips as MPs in the big cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' reads as the English city with its own MP; it is a tub. A whip is a party official who enforces voting discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub is filled from the faucet, so what fills it is the household supply from the mains.

clue.text: Love giving powers to regions, ignoring centre

indicators.note: ignoring the centre means the middle letters are left out

parts.note: devolution transfers powers from central government to regions

explanation.surface: A passion for handing power to the regions, bypassing central government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring centre' sounds like politics bypassing Westminster; it removes the two middle letters of the ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion is deep loyal affection and attachment to someone, a strong form of romantic feeling.

clue.text: One did a performance with tissue in nose

indicators.note: a performance puts on a show of something, so the preceding words are reworked into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the three words taken as raw letters

explanation.surface: Someone put on a show with a handkerchief up their nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tissue' suggests a paper hankie; it is body tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are a mass of lymphatic tissue at the back of the nasal cavity.

clue.text: Small figure but a lot of money

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the end is cut

parts.note: the American currency unit

explanation.surface: A tiny statuette that cost a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of money' reads as a fortune; it means most of a currency word.
explanation.definitionFit: A doll is a toy shaped like a miniature human, a little model person.

clue.text: Singer with slightly nasal tone

indicators.note: only a slight portion of the following words is used, the run tucked inside them

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A vocalist whose voice has a faintly nasal quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice part below soprano names the person who sings it, so it is a type of vocalist.

clue.text: Delightful sweet?

explanation.walkthrough: Together the two words evoke Angel Delight, a British instant whipped pudding, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means heavenly and lovely, and also describes a child who is innocent and good-natured.

clue.text: Signed pair

parts.note: surface reading: two people who have put their names to something, or a duo given a contract
setter's reading: the zodiac sign represented by a pair of twins

explanation.walkthrough: 'Signed' reads as autographed; it means made into a star sign, the one shown as the Twins.
explanation.definitionFit: The third astrological sign is symbolised by the twins Castor and Pollux, a couple in the zodiac.

clue.text: States introduction for the record

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A formal opening statement made for the minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a verb; it means the United States, flagging the American spelling of an opening section.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolog is the American spelling of prologue, the opening section that introduces a play or book.

clue.text: Tough court — extremely dry

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, the only letters kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sports court that is hard-wearing and bone dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a noun in the surface; it is the verb for romancing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody vegetables are fibrous and hard, so the word describes tough, stringy texture.

clue.text: King keeps the powerful leaderless from a distance

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: King Lear of Shakespeare's tragedy

indicators.note: with no leader means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the mighty are the powerful

explanation.surface: A monarch holds the strong at arm's length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From a distance' sounds like keeping away; 'from' is the link and 'a distance' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-year is an astronomical unit of length: how far light travels in one year.

clue.text: Fox solvers taken in and amused

definitions.note: in the sense amused oneself, played

indicators.note: something taken in is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: tod is an old dialect word for a fox
solvers are you, the readers, in old form ye

explanation.surface: Puzzlers are baffled by a tricky clue and find it funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' reads as a verb meaning baffle; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Toyed means played idly with something to pass the time, entertaining oneself casually.

clue.text: A question of trifles

definitions.note: describes a kind of quiz question, so works as a modifier
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the quiz category, as in a pub-quiz question about odd facts
second meaning: unimportant things, small details

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifles' tempts towards the layered British dessert; it means insignificant matters. The phrase reads as one, but splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are unimportant details, and quizzes built on such facts are called trivia questions.

clue.text: Compete with US Money Programme

parts.note: to compete in a game is to play
a bill is American paper money, a dollar bill

explanation.surface: Taking part in a TV show about American finance.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make 'Money Programme' look like a TV show title; 'Programme' alone is the definition, a theatre's printed one.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is the printed bill or programme for a theatre performance.

clue.text: Could be the lone conservation worker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the masked cowboy hero is the Lone one of these
second meaning: a warden who looks after a park or forest

explanation.walkthrough: The Lone Ranger is the masked hero of the old American western series.
explanation.definitionFit: A park warden patrolling woodland or a national park is employed to protect wildlife and landscape.

clue.text: Sex initially left out of intimacy clouds activity

indicators.note: initially means at first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so a letter standing for the side is removed

parts.note: cuddling is physical closeness
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Without sex, a closeness that is all fog and gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds are said to scud when the wind drives them quickly across the sky.
